topicName: Containerization, Multi-stage Docker Builds, and Kubernetes Deployment for .NET
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Containerization, Multi-stage Docker Builds, and Kubernetes Deployment for .NET"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern cloud-native .NET applications require efficient packaging, minimal security footprints, and robust orchestration. This tutorial covers building a production-ready .NET 8 Web API, optimizing its image size using multi-stage Docker builds, and deploying it to a Kubernetes cluster."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":".NET 8 SDK installed locally."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Docker Desktop installed and running."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Kubernetes cluster (Minikube, Docker Desktop Kubernetes, or cloud provider)."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Creating the .NET 8 Web API"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, create a new ASP.NET Core Web API project using the .NET CLI."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"dotnet new webapi -n DotNetK8sDemo
cd DotNetK8sDemo"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Writing a Multi-Stage Dockerfile"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Multi-stage builds allow you to use heavy SDK images for compiling and publishing the application, while copying only the lightweight compiled output into a secure, minimal runtime image. Create a file named Dockerfile in your root directory."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"# Stage 1: Build
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY ["DotNetK8sDemo.csproj", "./"]
RUN dotnet restore "DotNetK8sDemo.csproj"
COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish "DotNetK8sDemo.csproj" -c Release -o /app/publish /p:UseAppHost=false

# Stage 2: Runtime
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0 AS final
WORKDIR /app
EXPOSE 8080
COPY --from=build /app/publish .
USER app
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "DotNetK8sDemo.dll"]"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Building and Testing the Docker Image"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Build your Docker container image by running the following command in the terminal."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"docker build -t dotnet-k8s-demo:latest ."},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Test the container locally to verify it starts up successfully."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"docker run -d -p 8080:8080 --name demo-app dotnet-k8s-demo:latest"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Deploying to Kubernetes"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a deployment and service configuration file named deployment.yaml to define how Kubernetes runs your container."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: dotnet-demo-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: dotnet-demo
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: dotnet-demo
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: dotnet-demo
        image: dotnet-k8s-demo:latest
        imagePullPolicy: Never
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
--- 
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: dotnet-demo-service
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: dotnet-demo
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
      nodePort: 30080"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Apply the configuration to your Kubernetes cluster using kubectl."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml"},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Verifying the Deployment"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Check the status of your pods and services to ensure everything is running smoothly."},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"kubectl get pods
kubectl get services"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully containerized a .NET 8 application using multi-stage Docker builds and deployed it across a multi-replica Kubernetes cluster."}]
